subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should macOS Gateway LaunchAgents keep the canonical minimal PATH, add an explicit operator opt-in for user-bin directories, or include user-bin directories by default?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally harden the macOS service PATH, while the request improves Nix/Bun/local tool discovery and changes daemon command-resolution trust; automation should not choose that product/security tradeoff.

options.title: Keep default minimal, add explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current safe default and add a maintainer-approved service PATH opt-in only with docs, doctor/schema support, and security tests.

options.title: Change the macOS default
options.body: Include Darwin user-bin directories by default, accepting the broader command-resolution surface and requiring fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Decline service PATH expansion
options.body: Leave daemon PATH policy unchanged and direct users to tools.exec.pathPrepend, login-shell PATH behavior, or stable system install locations.

recommendation.title: Keep default minimal, add explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Preserve the current safe default and add a maintainer-approved service PATH opt-in only with docs, doctor/schema support, and security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the nearest explicit maintainer signal on adjacent managed service PATH precedence and authored recent package-path hardening commits.
